sessionName: Week 10 - Fee model and unit economics
summary: George Berrington modelled the economics with Paul and Rebecca. Gain-share earns higher margins but cash arrives up to 18 months after work starts. We agreed a margin target per fee type and to model three revenue scenarios.

discussion.keyPoints: Gain-share engagements averaged 52% margin against 34% for fixed fee. Rebecca pointed out the gain-share figure ignores the cost of waiting for cash.
Gain-share receivables stood at £780k. Paul accepted that this limits hiring.
Estimated cost to acquire a new client is £18k, mostly Paul's time.

recommendations.recommendation: Set minimum margins of 40% on fixed-fee and 50% on gain-share engagements.
Introduce a hybrid fee with a £20k upfront diagnostic credited against gain-share.
Model three scenarios for next year: £3.4m, £4.0m and £4.6m fees.
Reduce cost to acquire to £12k by moving outbound to Rebecca and the senior team.

nextFocus: Review the commercial model after one quarter of data.
nextPreparation: Rebecca to track margin by fee type for every new engagement.

tests.question: What minimum margins did we agree?
Is the hybrid fee with an upfront diagnostic agreed?
What revenue scenarios are we modelling?
